lines.text: In high-value manufacturing, enterprise systems constantly disagree.
Your ERP says 4,000 silicon-carbide power modules on PO-8841 shipped on time.
But warehouse dock scans show only 350 usable units, quality control quarantined 800 for solder voids, and ocean telemetry reports a 96-hour customs hold.
Meet Switchyard: an autonomous multi-agent reconciliation system that resolves cross-system conflicts before a $64,000/hr factory line stops.
Layer One is the Zetaris Data Harness.
Instead of brittle ETL pipelines, Switchyard queries ERP purchase orders, warehouse inventory ledgers, quality tickets, and live carrier feeds through single-statement Zetaris Lightning SQL.
Every query carries a fresh request UUID and maps conflicting records directly into a live provenance graph.
Layer Two runs all four Meterless Engines inside a non-linear adversarial loop.
When the Reconciler proposes a partial answer in Round One, the Conflict Critic rejects it for missing acoustic lab evidence and forces a targeted Round Two SQL re-query.

Scout Intent routes each task by blast radius, World Model enforces optimistic concurrency across 15 state transitions, Markovian compresses context tokens by 84%, and H-MEM commits supplier precedents across sessions.
Layer Three powers every agent through Meterless Nightshift on port 8088 using dual NVIDIA Nemotron lanes.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B handles low-latency SQL discovery, while Nemotron 3.5 Super 120B executes deep adversarial critique and policy verification, logging cryptographic model receipts on every turn.

Once all three conflicts are corroborated, Switchyard issues a sourced remediation order: releasing 350 verified units, rejecting the defective sub-lot, and splitting a 3,650-unit emergency order across Silicore Dresden and Pacific Semi.
Total impact: 85 hours of downtime prevented and $5.42M saved.
